description: Noise gate that replaces low-level passages with LITERAL DIGITAL ZEROS, in place (duration sample-exact: 110250 frames in -> 110250 frames out). Threshold semantics pinned against the binary and source (dev/standalone/gate.c): gatelevel is an ABSOLUTE level in dBFS (not peak-relative - a 0.005-amplitude segment is zeroed at -40 dB while a 0.02 segment survives, regardless of the file peaking at 0.25), and gating operates on CONTIGUOUS RUNS of samples whose |value| stays below the threshold - not on envelope windows. A run only becomes a gated region if it is longer than ~2 ms (interior; > 1 ms at the file edges): splicelen is hardcoded to 1 ms, and 1 ms fade-down/fade-up splices are applied at each region boundary, so the zero runs are click-free. Loud material is never touched: a full-scale sine's brief near-zero crossings are far shorter than 2 ms, so the file refuses with 'No signal is gateable' rather than distorting. Deterministic (identical decoded samples > 1.1 s apart). Mono only.
musical_use: THE UPSTREAM FIX FOR retime ON REAL RECORDINGS (the tranche-13 headline chain, verified end-to-end): retime's event modes detect silences as runs of EXACT zeros (tranche 11b - no threshold exists there), so any real recording with a noise floor reads as ONE event. Gate it first: a 2.5 s fixture with four bursts over a -54 dBFS noise floor went from 'WARNING: only 1 event found' (near-passthrough) to 'INFO: 4 events found' and a correct 120 MM retime after 'gate gate 1 in out -40'. Choose gatelevel between the noise floor and the quietest material you want to keep - the threshold is absolute, so read levels off the source, not off its peak. Beyond the retime chain: classic noise-floor cleanup between events, and a zero-run generator for anything downstream that keys on true silence (housekeep gate cuts at zero runs, sfedit-style silence logic). Use gate mode 2 (submode 2) to EXCISE the quiet passages instead of silencing them.

gatelevel.description: Absolute threshold in dBFS below which contiguous sample runs are zeroed (-40 = linear 0.01). CDP-enforced range -96 to 0: positive values and -97 refuse with 'Parameter[1] Value (...) out of range (-96.000000 to 0.000000)'. At 0 dB everything is below threshold and the run refuses 'Entire signal would be gated.'. Breakpoint refused ('Cannot read parameter 1 [...]: brkpnt_files not permitted.'). Scalar only.

examples.description: Make a real recording retime-compatible (the gate -> retime chain).
examples.expected_use: Noise floor between events becomes true digital zeros; retime modes 3-10 then see the events (verified: 4 events found vs 1 before gating). Pick a level above the floor, below the quietest event.
Only very quiet stretches longer than ~2 ms are zeroed; material above -60 dBFS is untouched (kept samples are bit-identical outside the 1 ms boundary splices).

known_issues: CONTENT REFUSALS (both verbatim, exit 255): 'ERROR: No signal is gateable' when no below-threshold run longer than the splice window exists (steady tones, flat noise beds - the shared duration fixture refuses exactly this way, so the findings duration row is null); 'ERROR: Entire signal would be gated.' when the whole file sits below the threshold.
Threshold is ABSOLUTE dBFS, not relative to the file's peak (pinned with a peak-0.25 fixture at -40 dB: 0.005-amplitude content zeroed, 0.02 kept). Set it from the source's real levels.

Gating is per-sample-run, not per-envelope-window: a below-threshold run must exceed 2 x 1 ms (interior; 1 ms at file edges) to be gated; shorter dips - including zero-crossings of loud material - are never touched. splicelen is hardcoded at 1 ms (source: gate.c line 1107).

MONO ONLY: stereo refuses 'File <name> is not of correct type (must be mono)'. The source contains dead multichannel code behind the check (a '**** THIS NEEDS TO BE FIXED ****' comment sits in the scan loop).

Kept regions are bit-identical to the source except the 1 ms boundary splices; zero regions are exact zeros - which is the whole point for retime (tranche 11b: retime counts silences as runs of samples == 0.0).
Duration static and sample-exact (frames preserved). Deterministic: two runs > 1.1 s apart produce identical decoded sha256.
